subject: Clarify: customer-specific log disposal acceptance and SIG checklist
messages:
From: Jamie Ellis <compliance@clearpathtx.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.inference>
Cc: sig@auditsigma.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Customer ask: longer debug-log retention + SIG rows clarified

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick chat earlier. To follow up: our security team is asking for two things before we proceed with the PO.

1) We need a written acceptance from Redwood that specific tenant-level debug logs (call traces and model-request payloads) can be retained for up to 90 days for our staging environment only. Our SOC 2 policy requires 90 days for incident investigations in non-prod environments.

2) SigmaAudit requested clarification on three SIG rows (A.9.2, R.3.4, and L.1.1) about how disposal is demonstrated for ephemeral logs. They prefer a short checklist and an artifact bundle rather than a long narrative.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide: (a) a single-paragraph formal acceptance letter for the 90-day staging exception, (b) a sample proof-of-delete manifest for S3 objects and (c) the SIG checklist template filled for the three rows? Also please attach any relevant CAIQ pointers.

Appreciate it — Jamie

----

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.inference>
To: Jamie Ellis <compliance@clearpathtx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, SigmaAudit intake <sig@auditsigma.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Customer ask: longer debug-log retention + SIG rows clarified

Jamie —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answer: we can support a scoped, tenant-specific exception for non-prod (staging) debug traces for up to 90 days provided three controls are in place:

- The retention applies only to a named tenant/environment (Clearpath-staging) and cannot be enabled at account-wide scope.
- Access is limited to an approved incident response role (RBAC), and all access is audited with immutable AuditTrail entries.
- Automated deletion is enforced via lifecycle rules; we will provide a proof-of-delete manifest after a scheduled purge.

I attached a draft single-paragraph acceptance letter and a sample S3 delete manifest (manifest includes object keys, timestamp, job id). The SIG rows were mapped into a concise checklist; see the attached XLSX (SIG-checklist-Clearpath-v2.xlsx).

Next steps I propose:
1) Jamie — review the attachments and confirm language is sufficient for your auditors.
2) Marissa — can you verify the RBAC scope and add the incident-role to the acceptance letter?
3) Karthik — can you generate the exact lifecycle rule JSON and confirmation script we’ll run for the first purge? I suggest we run the purge on Friday 2026-07-17 (non-peak) so we can capture the manifest and a signed DocuSign attestation.

If Jamie confirms, I’ll route the final acceptance note through legal and request a DocuSign.

— Priya

Signature:
Priya Natarajan
Manager, Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.inference>, Jamie Ellis <compliance@clearpathtx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Customer ask: longer debug-log retention + SIG rows clarified

All —

I reviewed Priya’s draft. RBAC scope looks good; incident-role name will be: incident-investigation@clearpath (limited to specific IAM group, no cross-tenant privileges). Karthik — please include that role in the lifecycle job's execution plan.

One operational note: we currently have a 30-day default TTL for ephemeral request traces in hosted. Enabling 90 days even for staging requires a small metadata flag on the tenant config and a validation step in our deploy pipeline to avoid accidental promotion to prod. I’ll coordinate with Infra to add that validation.

Jamie — from a procurement perspective, we usually attach a short addendum to the MSA accepting the exception and noting the controls. I can prepare the addendum language once the legal team confirms.

— Marissa

Signature:
Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SIG-checklist-Clearpath-v2.xlsx

----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.inference>, Jamie Ellis <compliance@clearpathtx.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Customer ask: longer debug-log retention + SIG rows clarified

Folks —

Per Priya/Marissa: I created the lifecycle job and a sample proof-of-delete manifest (attached s3-delete-manifest-20260714.txt). Key details:
- Job id: lifecycle-CP-4982-20260717
- Target prefix: customers/clearpath/staging/debug-traces/
- Pre-purge snapshot: saved to s3://redwood-evidence/CP-4982/prepurge-20260717.snap
- Deletion run: will execute 2026-07-17T02:00:00Z (non-peak)

I also generated a compact script that produces a signed manifest (SHA256 per object) that we can include in the DocuSign attestation. I attached the manifest sample and included a short checklist we will sign after purge.

Jamie — if you’re comfortable, we can schedule the purge and DocuSign attestation for Friday. If SigmaAudit requires additional artefacts (CAIQ mapping links), I can push them to the Drive folder listed above.

Thanks —
Karthik

Signature:
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Runtime Systems
Redwood Inference

Attachments: s3-delete-manifest-20260714.txt, docsign-approval-link.txt
